item.title: Judge Wetherell orders action in PEN America book removal case against Escambia schools
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A federal judge has directed action in the ongoing lawsuit brought by PEN American Center against the Escambia County School Board over book removals from school libraries. According to a court filing, Judge T. Kent Wetherell II has ordered action regarding a status report in the case, which challenges the school district's removal of books under…
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge has directed action in the ongoing lawsuit brought by PEN American Center against the Escambia County School Board over book removals from school libraries.

According to a court filing, Judge T. Kent Wetherell II has ordered action regarding a status report in the case, which challenges the school district's removal of books under Florida's HB 1069. The case, filed in federal court, centers on whether the district's removal practices violate free speech and other constitutional rights.

The specific details of what action the judge is requiring were not immediately clear from the court notice. PEN American Center, a national organization advocating for writers' and readers' rights, has been at the forefront of legal challenges to book removal policies across the country, including in Florida schools.

The Escambia County School Board has faced scrutiny over its book removal process in recent years, with dozens of titles challenged and removed from library shelves. The case is part of a broader national debate over school library materials and curriculum choices.

item.title: Escambia County Schools files status report in ongoing book removal lawsuit
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County School Board has filed a status report in its legal battle with PEN American Center over book removals from school libraries, according to court records. The filing was submitted October 16 in case CL67400156, which challenges the district's removal of books under Florida's HB 1069 legislation. PEN American Center, a nonprofit…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County School Board has filed a status report in its legal battle with PEN American Center over book removals from school libraries, according to court records. The filing was submitted October 16 in case CL67400156, which challenges the district's removal of books under Florida's HB 1069 legislation.

PEN American Center, a nonprofit organization advocating for free expression, sued the school board over the removals. The case is being heard in Florida state court by Judge T. Kent Wetherell II.

Court records show the district has been ordered to submit additional status reports, with the next deadline set for January 14, 2027. The case remains active as both sides continue to work through the legal process.

item.title: Sen. Scott pushes FCC to keep Chinese drone makers on security blacklist
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott is urging the Federal Communications Commission to maintain Chinese drone manufacturers DJI and Autel on its "Covered List" of communications equipment deemed a national security risk, according to a letter the Florida Republican sent to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr on Monday. Scott, who secured passage of the Countering CCP…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott is urging the Federal Communications Commission to maintain Chinese drone manufacturers DJI and Autel on its "Covered List" of communications equipment deemed a national security risk, according to a letter the Florida Republican sent to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr on Monday.

Scott, who secured passage of the Countering CCP Drones and Supporting Drones for Law Enforcement Act as part of last year's National Defense Authorization Act, argues both companies pose unacceptable security threats through data exfiltration to the Chinese Communist Party and unfair trade practices. "Not only do DJI and Autel present unacceptable national security risks through data exfiltration risks and their support to America's adversaries, but they have also been subsidized by the CCP, enabling them to destroy American manufacturing businesses," Scott wrote.

The senator contends that since 2015, China has flooded global markets with artificially low-priced drones from these manufacturers, driving American competitors out of business and undermining the U.S. drone supply chain. Scott's letter objects to the companies' legal challenges to their placement on the FCC's list, which effectively bans their products from U.S. markets. He has spent years pushing federal agencies to restrict Chinese drone technology from government and military use.

item.title: Early Voting Begins in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Early voting is underway in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties ahead of the Nov. 3 General Election. Voting began Monday morning and continues through Saturday, Oct. 31. Early-voting locations in both counties are open daily from 8 a.m. until 6 p.m. Escambia County has 10 early-voting sites, including the Supervisor of Elections Office in downtown…
item.content:encoded:
Early voting is underway in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties ahead of the Nov. 3 General Election.


Voting began Monday morning and continues through Saturday, Oct. 31.

Early-voting locations in both counties are open daily from 8 a.m. until 6 p.m.


Escambia County has 10 early-voting sites, including the Supervisor of Elections Office in downtown Pensacola, Main Library, Brownsville Community Center, Bellview Library, Southwest Library and the University of West Florida.


Additional Escambia locations are available at Asbury Place, the county Extension Services office in Cantonment, Molino Community Center and the Billy G. Ward Courthouse in Century.

Santa Rosa County has six locations available in Milton, Pace, Gulf Breeze and Navarre.

Unlike Election Day, voters do not have to use their assigned neighborhood precinct during early voting. Registered voters can cast a ballot at any early-voting site within the county where they are registered.


Voters should bring an accepted photo and signature identification.


The deadline to request that a vote-by-mail ballot be mailed to a Florida voter is 5 p.m. Thursday.


Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.

item.title: Plant City Sergeant Honored for Life-Saving CPR Response
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Plant City police sergeant has been recognized by Senator Ashley Moody for his quick thinking and lifesaving actions in September. Sgt. Billy Harvester responded to a call on September 19 for an unresponsive man at a residence. Upon arrival, Harvester found the man in cardiac arrest and immediately retrieved an AED (automated external…
item.content:encoded:
A Plant City police sergeant has been recognized by Senator Ashley Moody for his quick thinking and lifesaving actions in September.

Sgt. Billy Harvester responded to a call on September 19 for an unresponsive man at a residence. Upon arrival, Harvester found the man in cardiac arrest and immediately retrieved an AED (automated external defibrillator) from his patrol car. He applied the device, which delivered a shock to restore the man's heart rhythm, then performed CPR until the patient began breathing on his own.

Moody presented Harvester with a Florida's Finest Award, which recognizes law enforcement officers and citizens for extraordinary lifesaving efforts. "Law enforcement officers have to be ready to face anything when the call comes in—and Sgt. Harvester showed he was ready and capable," Moody said in a statement.

Harvester's decisive action—including his foresight to bring the AED into the residence before assessing the patient—proved critical to the man's survival. The patient's condition improved significantly before paramedics transported him from the scene.

item.title: Five Flags Speedway to Host 2027 Race for the Million Season Opener April 3
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Five Flags Speedway has been selected to kick off the 2027 Race for the Million (RFTM) 410 Winged Pavement Sprint Car Series on Saturday, April 3, marking the second consecutive year the Pensacola half-mile oval will launch the event. The series is billed as the richest pavement sprint car tour in history, with over $1 million in combined purse…
item.content:encoded:
Five Flags Speedway has been selected to kick off the 2027 Race for the Million (RFTM) 410 Winged Pavement Sprint Car Series on Saturday, April 3, marking the second consecutive year the Pensacola half-mile oval will launch the event. The series is billed as the richest pavement sprint car tour in history, with over $1 million in combined purse and championship awards across the season.

The announcement comes after a successful inaugural RFTM event at Five Flags last year. Five Flags Speedway General Manager Tim Bryant said the track's selection underscores its reputation as a premier destination venue. "Five Flags Speedway is one of the most historic and exciting tracks in the South, and we are thrilled that the Race for the Million will start right here in Pensacola for a second year," Bryant said in a statement.

The April 3 race will feature top-tier 410-winged sprint car drivers competing at speeds typical of short-track open-wheel racing. The event will receive global broadcast coverage through Racing America and RacingAmerica.TV, expanding the visibility of both the series and the local venue. Fans interested in tickets and additional event details can visit FiveFlagsSpeedway.com or follow the track on Facebook.

item.title: Baseball Hall of Famer Andre Dawson Receives Governor's Medal of Freedom
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis presented the Governor's Medal of Freedom to Baseball Hall of Famer Andre "The Hawk" Dawson on Monday, recognizing the Miami-born sports legend's distinguished 21-year major league career, his ongoing support of Florida A&M University, and his impact on the state. Dawson, who was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis presented the Governor's Medal of Freedom to Baseball Hall of Famer Andre "The Hawk" Dawson on Monday, recognizing the Miami-born sports legend's distinguished 21-year major league career, his ongoing support of Florida A&M University, and his impact on the state.

Dawson, who was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2010, played for the Montreal Expos, Chicago Cubs, Boston Red Sox, and Florida Marlins during his career. He earned eight All-Star selections, eight Gold Glove Awards, and four Silver Slugger Awards. His 1987 season with the Cubs was particularly memorable—he hit 49 home runs and drove in 137 runs to win the National League MVP award. He finished his career with 438 home runs, 2,774 hits, 1,591 RBIs, and 314 stolen bases.

A standout at Southwest Miami Senior High School, Dawson walked on to the Florida A&M baseball team after being unrecruited out of high school. His performance at the Tallahassee historically Black university caught the attention of MLB scouts, leading to his selection by the Montreal Expos in the 1975 draft and his 1976 debut. He earned National League Rookie of the Year honors in 1977.

Beyond his playing career, Dawson has remained committed to advancing opportunities for student-athletes at historically Black colleges and universities. In 2018, Major League Baseball renamed its annual HBCU baseball event the Andre Dawson Classic in recognition of his contributions. The Governor's Medal of Freedom is the highest honor the Governor can bestow upon a Floridian.

item.title: Florida Democrats to Challenge GOP Lawsuit Over Hope Florida Scandal Ad
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried will hold a virtual press conference Monday afternoon to respond to a Republican lawsuit seeking to remove a Democratic television advertisement about the Hope Florida scandal from the air. According to the Florida Democratic Party, the GOP filing — coming weeks before Election Day — is part of a broader…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried will hold a virtual press conference Monday afternoon to respond to a Republican lawsuit seeking to remove a Democratic television advertisement about the Hope Florida scandal from the air.

According to the Florida Democratic Party, the GOP filing — coming weeks before Election Day — is part of a broader campaign by Republicans to prevent public discussion of how $10 million in Medicaid settlement funds were diverted through a charity connected to the governor's wife and subsequently used to fund political activities.

The press conference is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. Monday and will be held virtually via Zoom. Interested media can RSVP through the FDP's online form or by emailing press@floridadems.org.

item.title: ECUA Executive Director Resigns Just Three Months After Taking Job
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority is undergoing another leadership change after Executive Director Jason Yarborough resigned just over three months after taking the job. The ECUA board voted 4-0 during a special meeting Friday to accept Yarborough's resignation. Yarborough submitted his resignation Wednesday. ECUA has not publicly announced a…
item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority is undergoing another leadership change after Executive Director Jason Yarborough resigned just over three months after taking the job.

The ECUA board voted 4-0 during a special meeting Friday to accept Yarborough's resignation.


Yarborough submitted his resignation Wednesday. ECUA has not publicly announced a reason for his departure.


Former ECUA Executive Director Bruce Woody is returning to the utility to serve as acting executive director and oversee daily operations during the transition.

ECUA engineer Brian Reed is handling the executive director's duties until Woody takes over.

Yarborough was selected earlier this year following a nationwide search and began serving as executive director in July.


Under a separation agreement, Yarborough will remain on paid administrative leave through Feb. 16.


The leadership change comes as ECUA continues Hurricane Isaias recovery operations and deals with a series of water-system disruptions and boil-water notices following the storm.

However, ECUA has not publicly linked those issues to Yarborough's resignation.

Woody previously led ECUA before retiring from the executive director position.


The ECUA board has not yet announced its longer-term plans for selecting the utility's next permanent executive director.

item.title: EREC Completes Power Restoration Nine Days After Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Escambia River Electric Cooperative says power restoration from Hurricane Isaias is complete after crews spent more than a week rebuilding damaged portions of the electrical system. The cooperative completed restoration Sunday night. Hurricane Isaias initially knocked out electricity to approximately 95 percent of EREC members in Escambia and…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia River Electric Cooperative says power restoration from Hurricane Isaias is complete after crews spent more than a week rebuilding damaged portions of the electrical system.

The cooperative completed restoration Sunday night.


Hurricane Isaias initially knocked out electricity to approximately 95 percent of EREC members in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.


Restoration in Escambia County was largely completed earlier in the recovery, while crews faced more extensive damage in portions of Santa Rosa County.


Hundreds of additional workers and pieces of equipment were brought into the area to help restore the system.


EREC's offices in Jay and Walnut Hill are also reopening Monday for the first time since the hurricane.


The cooperative is warning residents that damaged poles, wires and other electrical equipment may remain along roads and rights-of-way even though service has been restored. Crews will return to remove that equipment, and residents should not touch it.

Florida Power & Light was also nearing the end of its restoration effort over the weekend.

Late Sunday, FPL's outage system showed only a few dozen remaining outages across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.


Some remaining outages may involve homes or businesses that cannot safely be reconnected until privately owned electrical equipment damaged during the hurricane is repaired.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias Damage Tops $247 Million in Santa Rosa County
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Santa Rosa County's estimated damage from Hurricane Isaias has now surpassed $247 million as the county moves deeper into long-term recovery. The latest assessment is based on more than 3,800 damage reports submitted through the Santa Rosa County Property Appraiser's Office. County officials say more than 100 structures have been classified as…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County's estimated damage from Hurricane Isaias has now surpassed $247 million as the county moves deeper into long-term recovery.


The latest assessment is based on more than 3,800 damage reports submitted through the Santa Rosa County Property Appraiser's Office.

County officials say more than 100 structures have been classified as destroyed, while more than 400 suffered major damage. More than 1,000 sustained minor damage and more than 5,000 others were affected.


Altogether, more than 7,000 structures across Santa Rosa County have been impacted by the storm.


The damage estimate could continue to rise as additional reports are received.

Residents who have not yet reported hurricane damage are being encouraged to do so through the Property Appraiser's website. Property owners can search for their parcel and use the "Report Damage" option.


Cleanup is also continuing across the county.


As of Sunday, crews had collected more than 100,000 cubic yards of vegetative debris and more than 300 cubic yards of construction and demolition debris.

That's only a fraction of what's believed to be waiting for collection.


Santa Rosa County estimates Hurricane Isaias generated approximately 1.5 million cubic yards of debris. The county estimates debris removal alone could cost roughly $23 million.

Multiple collection passes are planned through affected neighborhoods.


Residents are being asked to keep vegetative debris separate from construction materials and place debris along the public right-of-way without blocking roads, drainage systems or fire hydrants.

item.title: Escambia County Extends Hurricane Isaias Emergency Until October 22
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County officials have extended the local state of emergency declaration for Hurricane Isaias through October 22, according to North Escambia. The extension allows the county to continue accessing operational funds for disaster response and ongoing cleanup efforts if needed. A local state of emergency gives county government flexibility to…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials have extended the local state of emergency declaration for Hurricane Isaias through October 22, according to North Escambia. The extension allows the county to continue accessing operational funds for disaster response and ongoing cleanup efforts if needed.

A local state of emergency gives county government flexibility to deploy resources and spend money quickly without the usual bureaucratic delays, which is critical during recovery operations following major storms. The declaration can be renewed again if cleanup work extends beyond next Wednesday.

Hurricane Isaias impacted Northwest Florida earlier this month, and the extension reflects the county's assessment that significant recovery work remains underway.

item.title: Escambia County Unemployment Dips to 4.7% as Leisure, Hospitality Lead Job Growth
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County's job market showed modest improvement in September, with the unemployment rate falling to 4.7% from 5.0% in August, according to data released Friday by the Florida Department of Commerce. The county has added 272 jobs so far this year, with leisure and hospitality sectors driving much of the recent growth. The decline in the…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County's job market showed modest improvement in September, with the unemployment rate falling to 4.7% from 5.0% in August, according to data released Friday by the Florida Department of Commerce.

The county has added 272 jobs so far this year, with leisure and hospitality sectors driving much of the recent growth. The decline in the jobless rate suggests steady if unspectacular momentum in local hiring as the fall season approaches.

These figures track employment trends across the broader Pensacola metropolitan area and reflect broader seasonal patterns typical for Northwest Florida's tourism and service-industry-dependent economy.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County voters can cast their ballots early starting today through October 31, ahead of the November 3 general election. Early voting runs from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily at 10 locations across the county.

Among the early voting sites are the Molino Community Center at 6450 Highway 95A and Escambia County Extension Services at 3740 Stefani Road in Cantonment. A complete list of all 10 voting locations is available through the Escambia County Supervisor of Elections office.

Voters who prefer to cast their ballots in person on Election Day can do so on November 3. For more information about polling locations, registration status, or ballot questions, visit the Escambia County Supervisor of Elections website or call their office.

item.title: Part-time Pensacola officer admits to decade-long pill buying scheme, FDLE says
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A part-time Pensacola Police Department officer has admitted to purchasing between 50 and 60 pills per week while wearing his police uniform over a 10-year period, according to a statement he provided to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. The officer was arrested on charges related to buying narcotics in uniform. The admission to FDLE…
item.content:encoded:
A part-time Pensacola Police Department officer has admitted to purchasing between 50 and 60 pills per week while wearing his police uniform over a 10-year period, according to a statement he provided to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

The officer was arrested on charges related to buying narcotics in uniform. The admission to FDLE investigators reveals the scope of the alleged illegal drug purchases, which authorities say spanned a decade.

Details about the officer's identity, the specific charges he faces, and the circumstances that led to the FDLE investigation have not yet been fully disclosed. The Pensacola Police Department has not released an official statement regarding the arrest or the officer's employment status.

item.title: Escambia County extends emergency declaration; residents push for faster debris removal after Hurricane Issa
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County commissioners have extended the local emergency declaration as the region continues recovery operations following Hurricane Issa, according to reporting from Citizen Portal News Florida. The extension keeps disaster protocols in place as cleanup and restoration efforts move forward across the county. Emergency declarations allow…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County commissioners have extended the local emergency declaration as the region continues recovery operations following Hurricane Issa, according to reporting from Citizen Portal News Florida.

The extension keeps disaster protocols in place as cleanup and restoration efforts move forward across the county. Emergency declarations allow local governments to mobilize resources, expedite spending, and coordinate mutual aid more efficiently during recovery phases.

However, residents have grown impatient with the pace of debris removal—a critical bottleneck in post-hurricane recovery. Homeowners and business owners are calling for the county to accelerate collection and hauling operations to clear streets and properties more quickly. Debris management after major hurricanes is typically one of the longest and most resource-intensive phases of disaster recovery, often competing with other urgent restoration needs for equipment and personnel.
